requirements.title: Method enum constants and static MethodSet factories
requirements.requirement: The system shall provide the public Java enum `Method` with exactly the constants `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS`, `TRACE` and `CONNECT`, in that declaration order, and the static factories `Method.get()`, `Method.any()` and `Method.of(Method...)`, each returning a `MethodSet`, with no instance method named after an HTTP method.
requirements.rationale: Covers D-030, D-031, D-032 (object.md §3.2).
acceptanceCriteria: `Method.values()` returns exactly `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS`, `TRACE`, `CONNECT` in this order. [D-030]

`Method.get()` returns a `MethodSet` containing only `GET`, `Method.of(Method.PUT, Method.PATCH)` returns a `MethodSet` containing exactly `PUT` and `PATCH`, and `Method.any()` returns a `MethodSet`; all three are static methods of `Method`. [D-031]

Reflection over `Method` finds no non-static method whose name is `get`, `head`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `options`, `trace` or `connect` (case-insensitive), so `Method.GET.delete()` does not compile. [D-032]

requirements.title: Immutable MethodSet combinators
requirements.requirement: The system shall provide the public immutable class `MethodSet` whose combinators `get()`, `head()`, `post()`, `put()`, `patch()`, `delete()` and `options()` each return a new set with that method added, and whose `except(Method)` returns a new set without the given method, every combinator leaving the receiver unchanged.
requirements.rationale: Covers D-033, D-034, D-035 (T01, T02 set parts).
acceptanceCriteria: For `MethodSet s = Method.get()`, calling `s.post()` returns a set containing `GET` and `POST`, and `s` still contains only `GET` afterwards; the same holds for every combinator and for `except`. [D-033]

`Method.get().delete().post()` contains exactly `GET`, `DELETE` and `POST`, and each of `get()`, `head()`, `post()`, `put()`, `patch()`, `delete()` and `options()` adds exactly its own constant to the receiver's members. [D-034]
`Method.get().post().except(Method.POST)` contains exactly `GET`, and `except` of a method that is not a member returns a set equal to the receiver. [D-035]
`MethodSet` has no public constructor or mutator, and its fields are final. [D-033]

requirements.title: Method.any() excludes TRACE and CONNECT
requirements.requirement: The system shall make `Method.any()` contain exactly `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` and `OPTIONS`, leaving out `TRACE` and `CONNECT` whatever router policy is in effect.
requirements.rationale: Covers D-036, D-037 (T02) and the wave decision on the TRACE/CONNECT policy (an enabled method is never part of `Method.any()`).
acceptanceCriteria: `Method.any()` contains exactly `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS` and contains neither `TRACE` nor `CONNECT`. [D-036]
`Method.any().except(Method.DELETE)` equals `Method.of(Method.GET, Method.HEAD, Method.POST, Method.PUT, Method.PATCH, Method.OPTIONS)`. [D-037]

`Method.any()` returns the same members when a router has `TRACE` and `CONNECT` routing enabled; `TRACE` or `CONNECT` enters a `MethodSet` only when named, as in `Method.of(Method.TRACE)`. [wave decision: TRACE/CONNECT policy]

requirements.title: MethodSet membership, ordered iteration and value equality
requirements.requirement: The system shall give `MethodSet` a membership accessor and an iteration accessor that yields members in `Method` declaration order, both named by the implementer (C-07) without Kotlin keywords, and value equality, so that two sets with the same members are equal and have equal hash codes.
requirements.rationale: Covers D-038, D-039 and the wave decision on `MethodSet` accessors (names decided in #2 under C-07, recorded in docs/api/routing.md; see the documentation requirement of this scope). Kotlin usability follows CLAUDE.md (object.md §12, T11).
acceptanceCriteria: The membership accessor returns true for every member and false for every other `Method` constant; the iteration accessor of `Method.of(Method.DELETE, Method.GET, Method.POST)` yields `GET`, `POST`, `DELETE` in that order. [D-038]
`Method.get().post()` equals `Method.of(Method.POST, Method.GET)` and both have the same `hashCode()`; sets with different members are not equal. [D-039]

No public method name of `Method` or `MethodSet` is a Kotlin hard keyword (`in`, `is`, `object`, `fun`, `when`, `val`, `var` and the rest of the hard keyword list), and a Kotlin test under `NaruServe-api/src/test/kotlin` calls `Method.get().post().except(Method.POST)` and both accessors without backticks and passes. [wave decision: MethodSet accessors]

requirements.title: Engine-free router with an opaque handler type
requirements.requirement: The system shall implement the router as engine-free code in `NaruServe-api` under package `com.snoworca.naruserve` or a subpackage, storing each registration with an opaque handler type parameter so that it compiles and is tested without `Request`, `Response`, `RouteHandler` or `RestApp`.
requirements.rationale: Covers D-059, D-389, and the wave decision note for wave 3 (D-422, D-442): the router receives the request path only; adapter handling of authority-form `CONNECT` and absolute-form targets belongs to wave 3. Depends on the wave 1 build checks (CON-BUILD-004, CON-BUILD-011, CON-BUILD-012, CON-BUILD-013).
acceptanceCriteria: The router classes live in `NaruServe-api/src/main/java` under `com.snoworca.naruserve` or a subpackage, and `./gradlew build` passes with the wave 1 `checkClassReferences` and animal-sniffer `android-api-level-21` checks covering them. [D-059]

The router type takes a handler type parameter, and a router test registers and looks up routes with a non-NaruServe handler type such as `String`, while `NaruServe-api` main contains no `Request`, `Response`, `RouteHandler` or `RestApp` type in wave 2. [D-389]
Public router types carry nullability annotations (the wave 1 JSpecify setup) on their public signatures. [CLAUDE.md Kotlin compatibility; C-03]

The lookup takes the request path (with an optional query string) and never parses an authority-form or absolute-form request target itself; that rewrite is left to the adapters. [wave decision: note for wave 3; D-442]

requirements.title: Route registration by method set and route kind
requirements.requirement: The system shall let the router register a handler for a `Method` or a `MethodSet`, a pattern and a route kind (HTTP or WebSocket), where one registration under a `MethodSet` serves every member method with the same handler and separate registrations under different methods on one pattern keep their own handlers.
requirements.rationale: Covers the router-level parts of T01 and T03, D-391 and the wave decision on route kind (each registration carries a route kind beside its opaque handler; WebSocket registrations go through an internal hook so wave 7 adds `app.ws` without changing the router).
acceptanceCriteria: After registering handler `h` for `Method.get().delete().post()` on `/items`, lookups of `GET`, `DELETE` and `POST` `/items` each return the matched result with handler `h`. [T01]
After registering `h1` for `GET` and `h2` for `DELETE` on `/users/:id`, a `GET /users/1` lookup returns `h1` and a `DELETE /users/1` lookup returns `h2`. [T03]

A WebSocket registration is made through a hook that marks the pattern as WebSocket and is not part of any public `RestApp` API in wave 2; the matched result names the route kind of the registration it returns. [D-391; wave decision: route kind]

requirements.title: Route pattern syntax and registration-time validation
requirements.requirement: The system shall accept route patterns made of literal segments and `:name` variable segments, where a variable matches exactly one non-empty path segment and never crosses `/`, and shall fail registration with a configuration error for a pattern that contains Express wildcard or regular-expression syntax, an empty variable name, a variable name repeated within the pattern, or an empty segment.
requirements.rationale: Covers D-047, D-048, the wave decision on pattern validation (empty or repeated variable name is a configuration error at registration time) and the loop W residual (a pattern containing an empty segment such as `/a//b` is a configuration error). Reporting the empty-segment error at registration, together with the other pattern errors, is the implementer's choice under C-07.
acceptanceCriteria: `/users/:id` matches `/users/42` with `id` = `42`, and matches neither `/users`, `/users/` nor `/users/42/posts`. [D-047]
Registering a pattern containing `?`, `*`, `+`, `(` or `)` fails with a configuration error. [D-048]
Registering `/a/:` or `/a/:id/:id` fails with a configuration error at registration time. [wave decision: pattern validation]
Registering `/a//b` fails with a configuration error, while `/` and a pattern with one trailing slash such as `/users/` are accepted. [loop W residual: empty segment]

requirements.title: Engine-free request path validator
requirements.requirement: The system shall provide an engine-free path validator, run before the router lookup by the wave 3 dispatcher and every adapter, that inspects the raw request path without decoding it and rejects malformed percent-encoding, percent-encoded bytes that are not valid UTF-8, raw non-ASCII characters, an encoded `/`, an encoded or raw `NUL`, and any `.` or `..` segment in raw or percent-encoded form, matching the rules TinyHttpd's parser applies.
requirements.rationale: Covers D-052 and the wave decision on path validation before lookup (W2-003, W2-004), plus the loop W residual (the validator inspects the raw path and does not decode it). Mapping a rejection to `400` is the wave 3 dispatcher's job; the router lookup returns only the six results of D-390.
acceptanceCriteria: The validator rejects `/a%2`, `/a%zz`, `/a%C3` (truncated UTF-8), `/a%FF`, a path containing a raw character above U+007F, `/a%2Fb`, `/a%2fb`, `/a%00`, a path containing a raw U+0000, `/./a`, `/a/..`, `/a/%2e`, `/a/%2E%2e` and `/a/.%2e/b`. [D-052]
The validator accepts `/users/42`, `/files/%252e`, `/caf%C3%A9` and `/a/.hidden`, and its result is the same whether or not a query string follows the path. [D-052; D-051]

The validator returns an accept or reject decision without returning a decoded path, and the router lookup API has no result variant for a rejected path. [loop W residual; wave decision: path validation before lookup]

requirements.title: Strict default matching with single percent-decoding
requirements.requirement: The system shall match a request path against patterns ignoring the query string, decoding each path segment exactly once, and by default comparing case-sensitively with a significant trailing slash and with an empty segment never matching a literal or variable segment, returning path parameter values as decoded once and otherwise as received.
requirements.rationale: Covers D-049, D-050, D-051, the wave decision on the path-form policy (strict default; parameter values always as received) and the loop W residual (the router decodes path segments exactly once when it extracts parameters, D-051, D-399).
acceptanceCriteria: `/users?id=1` and `/users` both match `/users`. [D-049]
Under the default policy `/Users` and `/users/` do not match `/users`, and `/users/` matches only a pattern registered as `/users/`. [D-050]
`/files/%252e` matched against `/files/:name` yields `name` = `%2e`, and `/caf%C3%A9` matches the literal pattern `/café`. [D-051]
Under the default policy `/a//b` matches neither `/a/:x/b` nor `/a/b` and reaches the no-match result when no other pattern matches. [wave decision: path-form policy]

requirements.title: Path-form router policies
requirements.requirement: The system shall provide three independent router policy switches, each off by default, that merge repeated slashes, ignore one trailing slash, and compare literal segments case-insensitively, with path parameter values returned as received under every switch and the configuration API names on `RestApp` left to wave 3.
requirements.rationale: Covers D-053 and the wave decision on the path-form policy (D-050, D-053, D-070); the RestApp-level names are decided in wave 3 (D-398).
acceptanceCriteria: With repeated-slash merging on, `/a//b` matches `/a/b`; with it off, it does not. [D-053]

With trailing-slash ignoring on, `/users/` matches `/users` and `/users` matches a pattern registered as `/users/`; `/users//` does not match `/users` unless repeated-slash merging is also on. [D-053]
With case-insensitive matching on, `/USERS/Bob` matches `/users/:name` and yields `name` = `Bob`. [D-053; wave decision: path-form policy]
Each switch can be set without the others, and a router built without setting any of them behaves as the strict default. [wave decision: path-form policy]

requirements.title: Per-method pattern priority
requirements.requirement: The system shall, for the request method, pick the most specific matching pattern among the routes of that method, comparing patterns segment by segment from the left so that the first differing segment decides and a literal segment beats a variable segment regardless of registration order.
requirements.rationale: Covers D-054, D-055 (T04) and the wave decision on per-method priority (as in Express).
acceptanceCriteria: With `GET /users/:id` registered before `GET /users/me`, a `GET /users/me` lookup returns the `/users/me` handler and `GET /users/42` returns the `/users/:id` handler; the result is the same with the opposite registration order. [D-054]
With `GET /a/:x/c` and `GET /a/b/:y`, a `GET /a/b/c` lookup returns the `/a/b/:y` handler. [D-055]
With `GET /users/me` and `DELETE /users/:id`, a `DELETE /users/me` lookup returns the matched result for `DELETE /users/:id`. [wave decision: per-method priority]

requirements.title: Conflict detection at route-table freeze
requirements.requirement: The system shall provide a route-table freeze, which wave 4 calls inside `listen()` before any socket is bound, that raises a configuration error naming both conflicting registrations when two registrations of the same route kind share a method and have the same pattern or patterns that differ only in variable names, comparing patterns normalised under the active path-form policies, and when a `TRACE` or `CONNECT` route is registered while that method's routing is disabled.
requirements.rationale: Covers D-056, D-057, D-058 (T03) and the loop W residual (conflict detection on policy-normalised patterns; a TRACE or CONNECT route while disabled is a configuration error at freeze). A WebSocket route and a `GET` route on one pattern do not conflict (D-068).
acceptanceCriteria: Registering `GET /a` twice, or `GET /a` and a `MethodSet` registration containing `GET` on `/a`, makes the freeze raise a configuration error. [D-056]
Registering `GET /a/:x` and `GET /a/:y` makes the freeze raise a configuration error, while `GET /a/:x` and `POST /a/:y` freeze without error. [D-057]
The configuration error message names the method and the pattern of both conflicting registrations, and registration itself does not raise it before the freeze. [D-058]

With case-insensitive matching on, `GET /Users` and `GET /users` conflict at freeze; with trailing-slash ignoring on, `GET /a` and `GET /a/` conflict; under the strict default neither pair conflicts. [loop W residual: normalised conflicts]

Registering a `TRACE` route while `TRACE` routing is disabled makes the freeze raise a configuration error, and likewise for `CONNECT`; a WebSocket registration and a `GET` registration on the same pattern freeze without error. [loop W residual; D-068]

requirements.title: Lookup result contract and precedence
requirements.requirement: The system shall make a route lookup, which takes the raw method token, the request path and an upgrade flag, return an engine-free result that is exactly one of matched (handler, path parameters, actual method, route kind, automatic-`HEAD` flag), method mismatch (with an `Allow` set), automatic OPTIONS (with an `Allow` set), WebSocket-only, unsupported method or no match, chosen in this order: unsupported method; no match; matched; automatic OPTIONS; automatic `HEAD`; WebSocket-only; method mismatch.
requirements.rationale: Covers D-390 and the wave decision on lookup result order (D-060..D-069); the route kind on the matched result follows the wave decision on route kind.
acceptanceCriteria: The result type exposes exactly six kinds and each lookup returns exactly one; the matched kind carries the handler, the path parameters, the actual method, the route kind and the automatic-`HEAD` flag, and the method-mismatch and automatic-OPTIONS kinds carry an `Allow` `MethodSet`. [D-390]

An unrecognised method token yields unsupported method even when no pattern matches the path, and a recognised method on a path no pattern matches yields no match. [wave decision: lookup result order]
On a matched path a route of the request method wins over automatic OPTIONS and automatic `HEAD`, which win over WebSocket-only, which wins over method mismatch. [wave decision: lookup result order]

requirements.title: No-match result
requirements.requirement: The system shall return the no-match result for a recognised, routable method when no pattern of any route kind matches the path, including an `OPTIONS` request to such a path.
requirements.rationale: Covers D-060 (T06) and the wave decision on lookup result order (`OPTIONS` to an unmatched path is no match; `OPTIONS *` stays with D-442 in wave 3).
acceptanceCriteria: With only `GET /users` registered, `GET /nope` yields no match. [D-060]
With only `GET /users` registered, `OPTIONS /nope` yields no match, not automatic OPTIONS. [wave decision: lookup result order]
A path that matches only a WebSocket pattern is not a no-match path for any method. [wave decision: lookup result order]

requirements.title: Method-mismatch result and Allow set
requirements.requirement: The system shall return the method-mismatch result when the path matches but no route of the request method matches it and no earlier result applies, carrying an `Allow` set that is the union of the methods of every route whose pattern matches the path, plus `HEAD` wherever `GET` is present and `OPTIONS` always, with a WebSocket route counted as `GET`.
requirements.rationale: Covers D-061 (T02, T06) and the wave decision on `Allow` sets.
acceptanceCriteria: With `Method.any().except(Method.DELETE)` registered on `/r`, `DELETE /r` yields method mismatch with `Allow` = `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `OPTIONS`. [D-061; T02]
With `POST /a/:id` and `GET /a/me`, `PUT /a/me` yields method mismatch with `Allow` = `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `OPTIONS`. [wave decision: Allow sets]
With only `POST /p`, `GET /p` yields method mismatch with `Allow` = `POST`, `OPTIONS` (no `HEAD`). [wave decision: Allow sets]
With a WebSocket route and a `POST` route on `/w`, `PUT /w` yields method mismatch whose `Allow` contains `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST` and `OPTIONS`. [wave decision: Allow sets]

requirements.title: Automatic HEAD resolution
requirements.requirement: The system shall resolve a `HEAD` request for which no `HEAD` route matches the path to the most specific matching `GET` route, returned as matched with the automatic-`HEAD` flag set, and shall give a matching explicit `HEAD` route precedence over this resolution.
requirements.rationale: Covers D-062, D-063 (T05) and the wave decision on lookup result order (a route of the request method is matched first). The `req.method()` value during automatic `HEAD` is decided in wave 3 (D-398).
acceptanceCriteria: With only `GET /x`, `HEAD /x` yields matched with the `GET` handler, actual method `GET` and the automatic-`HEAD` flag set. [D-062]
With `GET /x` and `HEAD /x`, `HEAD /x` yields matched with the `HEAD` handler and the flag clear. [D-063]
With `HEAD /x/:id` and `GET /x/me`, `HEAD /x/me` yields the `HEAD /x/:id` route with the flag clear. [wave decision: per-method priority]

requirements.title: Automatic OPTIONS result
requirements.requirement: The system shall return the automatic-OPTIONS result, carrying the same `Allow` set as the method-mismatch result, for an `OPTIONS` request to a matched path when no `OPTIONS` route matches it, and shall give a matching explicit `OPTIONS` route precedence.
requirements.rationale: Covers D-064, D-065 (T05) and the wave decision on `Allow` sets.
acceptanceCriteria: With `GET /x` and `POST /x`, `OPTIONS /x` yields automatic OPTIONS with `Allow` = `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `OPTIONS`. [D-064]
With `GET /x` and `OPTIONS /x`, `OPTIONS /x` yields matched with the `OPTIONS` handler. [D-065]
With only a WebSocket route on `/w`, `OPTIONS /w` yields automatic OPTIONS with `Allow` = `GET`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`. [wave decision: Allow sets]

requirements.title: Unsupported-method result for unknown tokens
requirements.requirement: The system shall match the raw method token against `Method` constant names exactly and case-sensitively and return the unsupported-method result, whatever the path, for every token that is not a `Method` constant name.
requirements.rationale: Covers D-066 (T06) and the loop W residual (`get` is not `GET`; every other token is unsupported method, `501`).
acceptanceCriteria: With `GET /x` registered, tokens `FOO`, `get` and `Get` on `/x` yield unsupported method. [D-066; loop W residual]
Token `PROPFIND` on a path no pattern matches yields unsupported method, not no match. [wave decision: lookup result order]

requirements.title: TRACE and CONNECT enable policy
requirements.requirement: The system shall disable `TRACE` and `CONNECT` routing by default, so that both yield the unsupported-method result whatever the path, and shall provide a router policy that enables each of them separately, after which an enabled method routes like any other method and is registered only by naming it.
requirements.rationale: Covers D-067, D-070 and the wave decision on the TRACE/CONNECT policy. On the TinyHttpd adapter the policy also governs a `CONNECT` with an origin-form or absolute-form target; authority-form `CONNECT` is answered `501` by TinyHttpd before dispatch (deferred TinyHttpd gap under D-020, wave 3).
acceptanceCriteria: Under the default policy, `TRACE /x` and `CONNECT /x` yield unsupported method whether or not any route matches `/x`. [D-067]

With only `TRACE` enabled, a registered `TRACE /x` route is matched, `TRACE /y` with no matching pattern yields no match, `TRACE` on a path with only a `GET` route yields method mismatch, and `CONNECT /x` still yields unsupported method. [wave decision: TRACE/CONNECT policy]

With `CONNECT` enabled, `CONNECT` behaves as `TRACE` does in the previous criterion, and in neither case does a registration under `Method.any()` serve the enabled method. [wave decision: TRACE/CONNECT policy; D-036]

requirements.title: WebSocket route resolution and the upgrade flag
requirements.requirement: The system shall resolve a lookup with the upgrade flag set against WebSocket routes first and a lookup without it against HTTP routes only, so that a WebSocket route and a `GET` route coexist on one pattern, and shall provide an engine-free helper that sets the upgrade flag only for a `GET` whose `Connection` header carries the `upgrade` token and whose `Upgrade` header carries the `websocket` token, both compared case-insensitively within comma-separated lists.
requirements.rationale: Covers D-068 and the wave decision on route kind, plus the loop W residual on the upgrade flag (any other `Upgrade` value, or a `websocket` upgrade on another method, is an ordinary request).
acceptanceCriteria: With a `GET` route and a WebSocket route on `/chat`, a `GET /chat` lookup with the upgrade flag yields the WebSocket route and without the flag yields the `GET` route, each matched result naming its route kind. [D-068]

The helper sets the flag for `GET` with `Connection: keep-alive, Upgrade` and `Upgrade: WebSocket`, and clears it for `Upgrade: h2c`, for a missing `Connection` upgrade token, and for `POST` with both headers. [loop W residual: upgrade flag]
A WebSocket pattern is never matched by a lookup without the upgrade flag. [wave decision: route kind]

requirements.title: WebSocket-only result
requirements.requirement: The system shall return the WebSocket-only result, which the wave 3 dispatcher answers with `426 Upgrade Required` carrying `Upgrade: websocket` and `Connection: Upgrade`, for a `GET` or `HEAD` without the upgrade flag to a path whose matching routes include a WebSocket route but no HTTP `GET` route, and for any other request without the upgrade flag to a path whose only matching routes are WebSocket routes, unless an earlier result applies.
requirements.rationale: Covers D-069 and the loop W residual (plain `GET` or `HEAD` to a path with a WebSocket route but no HTTP `GET` route is WebSocket-only, consistent with the `Allow` set counting the WebSocket route as `GET`), together with the wave decision on lookup result order. The `426` response is asserted end to end in wave 7.
acceptanceCriteria: With only a WebSocket route on `/w`, `GET /w` and `HEAD /w` without the flag and `POST /w` yield WebSocket-only, and `OPTIONS /w` yields automatic OPTIONS. [D-069; wave decision: lookup result order]
With a WebSocket route and a `POST` route on `/w`, `GET /w` and `HEAD /w` without the flag yield WebSocket-only and `POST /w` yields matched. [loop W residual]
With a WebSocket route and an HTTP `GET` route on `/w`, `GET /w` without the flag yields the matched `GET` route, and `HEAD /w` yields automatic `HEAD`. [D-068; D-069]

requirements.title: Upgrade request without a WebSocket route falls back to GET
requirements.requirement: The system shall resolve a lookup with the upgrade flag set whose path matches no WebSocket pattern as an ordinary `GET` without upgrading, reaching the path's `GET` route or else the method-mismatch or no-match result.
requirements.rationale: Covers D-441 (loop D fix V2-005) and the wave decision on route kind.
acceptanceCriteria: With only `GET /g`, a `GET /g` lookup with the upgrade flag yields matched with the `GET` handler and route kind HTTP. [D-441]
With only `POST /p`, a `GET /p` lookup with the upgrade flag yields method mismatch. [D-441]
With no route matching `/none`, a `GET /none` lookup with the upgrade flag yields no match. [D-441]

requirements.title: Decided routing semantics in docs/api/routing.md
requirements.requirement: The system shall record in `docs/api/routing.md` the routing semantics decided in wave 2 and the `MethodSet` membership and iteration accessors with Java and Kotlin examples, keeping the (미확정) markers that name configuration APIs and the marker on the `req.method()` value during automatic `HEAD` for wave 3.
requirements.rationale: Covers D-070, the wave decision on markers (D-070, D-398) and the wave decision on `MethodSet` accessors (D-038). Follows CLAUDE.md: Express correspondence and Java and Kotlin examples per API.
acceptanceCriteria: `docs/api/routing.md` describes the `//`, trailing-slash and case policy switches and their strict default, the `TRACE`/`CONNECT` enable policy, the `Allow` set rule, the lookup result order including WebSocket-only and the upgrade fallback, without naming configuration API methods. [D-070]
`docs/api/routing.md` names the `MethodSet` membership and iteration accessors exactly as implemented, with a Java and a Kotlin example each. [D-038; wave decision: MethodSet accessors]

The (미확정) markers on the configuration API names (lines on `TRACE`/`CONNECT` and on `//`/trailing slash/case) and on the `req.method()` value during automatic `HEAD` remain, and no marker is added for a semantic that wave 2 decided. [wave decision: markers]
